Agent Access Model: Give agents task-specific, short-lived credentials enforced at the harness, instead of inheriting a human's standing access.
Agent Fleet Dashboards: Supervise many running agents at once: status, blockers, token burn, and fast attach into any session.
Agent-Runtime-as-a-Service Substrates: Vendors selling an agent its own hosted sandbox: isolated execution plus state that survives between runs.
Agentic Code Quality: Move the quality gate out of human review and into the environment itself — tests, thresholds, automated checks.
Autonomous Work Loops: Scheduled and self-pacing loops that keep work moving: nightly jobs, recurring scans, watchers that act on changes.
Cache-Stable Agent Thread Architecture: Structure a long thread so the prompt cache keeps hitting: stable prefix, append-only history, deferred tools.
Composable Tests: Build suites from small orthogonal tests that compose, rather than overlapping assertions across similar cases.
Computer-Use Verification for Coding Age: Let the agent drive the real UI to verify its own work, and attach the evidence to the pull request.
Context Management via Subagents: Delegate self-contained work to subagents that burn their own context and return only conclusions.
Deterministic Agent Workflows: Freeze a proven multi-step pattern into versioned code, so later runs execute instead of re-reasoning.
Domain-Driven Agents: Make a legacy codebase legible to agents by applying domain-driven design to it, rather than by upgrading the model.
Fine-Tuning Open-Weight Models: Put tribal knowledge in the weights instead of re-injecting it into context every session.
Fresh-Context Review Agents: Review with an agent that sees only the artifact, never the conversation that produced it.
Hedged LLM Requests: Fire the same request twice in parallel, take whichever returns first, cancel the loser.
Knowledge Compressor: Compress technical documentation for model consumption before it ever reaches an agent's context.
Knowledge-Injection Hooks: Hooks that check a knowledge base on every prompt and inject what is relevant before the agent runs.
Low-Cost Model Swarms: Many cheap models in structured collaboration — voting, cross-review — betting orchestration substitutes for model strength.
Model Routing: Send each request to the cheapest model that can handle it, reserving frontier models for hard reasoning.
Multi-Agent Debate: Several agents propose and challenge each other's answers from different angles until they converge.
Plan-First Development: Always produce and review a plan before the agent writes any code.
Proactive Memory Agents: Counter behavioural state decay on long tasks by resurfacing requirements before the agent drifts off them.
Programming Language Choice for Coding A: Whether the language a repo is written in measurably changes coding-agent performance.
Revision Prompting: When the input changes slightly, send the diff and the old output instead of regenerating from scratch.
Self-Improving Agent Harnesses: Agents that read their own transcripts and propose changes to their own rules, tools and skills.
Skills vs MCP Servers: Swap always-loaded MCP tool definitions for progressively-loaded skills plus plain scripts.
Specula: Auto-derive TLA+ specifications from code, model-check them for concurrency bugs, and reproduce what it finds.
Speculative Programmatic Tool Calling: Start executing a tool call before the model has finished deciding it needs one.
Task Runners for Coding Tasks: Give every repo one command surface — just test, just build — instead of stack-specific incantations.
Task vs Job Delegation: The task is not the job: cheap execution exposes what delegating the implementation leaves undone.
